confirmed_defect.counterexample: For every target Sigma in F_p(M), the constant zero matrix estimator is Borel and has squared operator loss ||Sigma||²<=M² deterministically under every Huber contaminant. Fix any proposed positive threshold coefficient C_M and choose n=1 and integer p>M²/C_M; then the proposed lower event is empty, contradicting any positive probability lower bound.

complete_extension_argument.large_sample_large_ratio: If p/n>c and n>=2/c, set k=floor(cn), so1<=k<=p andc/2<=k/n<=c. For zero-padding isometry J:R^k→R^p, each Θ∈F_k(M) embeds as JΘJᵀ∈F_p(M), and the centered Gaussian sample is J times the k-dimensional sample. For arbitrary Borel ambient matrix estimator A, the map B(y)=Jᵀ A(Jy_1,...,Jy_n)J is Borel, including nonsymmetric actions. The norm definition gives ||Jᵀ(A-JΘJᵀ)J||op<=||A-JΘJᵀ||op. Apply the already established small-ratio lower bound in dimensionk to B: ambient tail probability>=c at thresholdbk/n>=bc/2>=a_M min{1,p/n}.
complete_extension_argument.remaining_small_samples: If p/n>c andn<2/c, take Σ0=(M/2)I_p and Σ1=Σ0+h e1e1ᵀ, h=M√c/4. They are positive definite in F_p(M), with separationh. For t=2h/M, the actual Gaussian KL supplier gives KL(P0||P1)=1/2[log(1+t)+(1+t)^-1-1]<=t²/4=h²/M²; integrating derivative t/(1+t)²<=t proves the inequality. ProductKL<=nh²/M²<1/8, so actual Pinsker gives TV<=1/4. Classify any estimator by nearest covariance, fixed-index ties. This Borel binary rule, with scalar targets0,1, has squared risks equal to error probabilities. Actual expected-risk LeCam theorem therefore gives maxerror>=(1-TV)/8>=3/32>=c. A wrong classification forces operator error>=h/2, giving squared tail thresholdh²/4=M²c/64>=a_M min{1,p/n}.
complete_extension_argument.contamination: The existing covariance modulus is >=d_M epsilon² and finite. The ambient-action lemma withM0=a_M min{1,p/n} yields threshold1/16 max(M0,omega) and probabilitymin(c,1/2). This threshold dominates a fixed positive constant times max(min{1,p/n},epsilon²)=min{1,max(p/n,epsilon²)} for0<=epsilon<=1. It covers all Borel ambient matrix actions.

Use the median-of-means pilot $\hat\mu$, grid $\sigma_j=2^j\sigma_{min}$, $\theta_j=\sigma_j^{-1}\sqrt{\beta/m}$, on $\mathcal J=\{j\in\mathbb Z:\sigma_{min}\le\sigma_j<2\sigma_{max}\}$, and Lepski selection of the smallest index whose estimates agree with all larger-scale candidates within $6\sigma_k\sqrt{\beta/m}$. Under finite matrix variance $\sigma_0^2=\|E[\|X-\mu\|^2(X-\mu)(X-\mu)^T]\|>0$, $d=\sigma_0^2/\|\Sigma_0\|^2$, $m\ge C d\beta$ for $\beta>1$, and preliminary bracket $0<\sigma_{min}\le\sigma_0\le\sigma_{max}$, `thm-heavy-tailed-covariance-bound` gives $\|\hat\Sigma^*-\Sigma_0\|_{op}\le18\sigma_0\sqrt{\beta/m}$ with probability at least $1-5d\log_2(2\sigma_{max}/\sigma_{min})e^{-\beta}$; its proof combines the matrix truncation deviation, median-of-means pilot and Lepski selection. No arbitrary-contamination guarantee follows from finite matrix variance. B: dense Huber, block-sparse Huber and clean finite-matrix-variance examples. | F06 complete.
